findings.title: add_members/remove_member require :group_id but the route only supplies :id
findings.body: The routes added in config/routes.rb (`delete "members" => "groups#remove_member"` and `put "members" => "groups#add_members"`, lines 49-50) are declared directly inside the `resources :groups do ... end` block without being wrapped in an explicit `member do ... end` block or `on: :member`. Such bare declarations resolve to member routes using the resource's default id parameter, i.e. the URL becomes `/admin/groups/:id/members` with the captured param named `id`, not `group_id` (this matches the previous `get "users"` route it replaced, and matches the JS which builds the URL as `/admin/groups/' + this.get('id') + '/members.json'`, embedding the id directly in the path). However `add_members` (line 66) and `remove_member` (line 85) both call `params.require(:group_id)`. Since the real request will only populate `params[:id]`, every real HTTP call to these endpoints will raise `ActionController::ParameterMissing` (400) instead of succeeding, completely breaking the admin 'add members' / 'remove member' feature that this PR is supposed to deliver, even though it looks correct in isolation.

findings.title: Controller specs bypass routing and mask the group_id/:id param mismatch
findings.body: The specs for `.add_members` and `.remove_member` (e.g. `xhr :put, :add_members, group_id: 1, usernames: "l77t"` at line 94 and `xhr :delete, :remove_member, group_id: group.id, user_id: user.id` at line 125) inject `group_id` straight into the controller action, bypassing the actual route path/param extraction defined in config/routes.rb. Because of this, the tests pass even though the real route (a bare member-style declaration generating `/admin/groups/:id/members`) would never populate `params[:group_id]` for an actual HTTP request. There is no request-spec/feature-level test that exercises the real route, so the production-breaking parameter mismatch described above is not caught by this test suite.

findings.title: Public group members page now silently truncates to 50 members with no pagination UI
findings.body: `members` previously returned the full, unpaginated list of users for non-automatic groups and only limited automatic groups to 200. This PR unconditionally applies `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` / `offset = params[:offset].to_i` to every group (lines 22-26), and `Discourse.Group#findMembers` (app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js) defaults `limit` to 50. The public-facing group members page (`app/assets/javascripts/discourse/templates/group/members.hbs` + `discourse/routes/group-members.js.es6`) was not given any next/previous controls (unlike the admin template, which did get pagination UI). As a result, any group (automatic or not) with more than 50 members will now show only the first 50 members on the public `/groups/:name/members` page with no way to see the rest, a functional regression compared to the previous behavior for non-automatic groups (which showed all members).

findings.title: findMembers() failures are now silently swallowed
findings.body: Previously `afterModel` returned the promise from `model.findMembers()`, so a failed request (e.g. network/server error) would reject the route's model hook and trigger Ember's normal error substate handling. Now `setupController` just calls `model.findMembers();` without returning or handling the resulting promise (same pattern in app/assets/javascripts/discourse/routes/group-members.js.es6, lines 8-12). If the members request fails, there is no error feedback to the user and the member list simply stays empty/stale with no indication that something went wrong.

findings.title: Username input is not cleared after adding members, and failures are unhandled
findings.body: The `addMembers` action contains an acknowledged `// TODO: should clear the input` and calls `this.get("model").addMembers(this.get("usernames"))` without handling the returned promise's rejection. Similarly `removeMember` (lines 51-59) calls `self.get("model").removeMember(member)` without a `.catch`. If the add/remove request fails server-side (e.g. validation error), the admin gets no feedback and, for addMembers, the previously entered usernames remain in the input, which can lead to accidental duplicate submissions or user confusion. This should be resolved before merge rather than left as an open TODO.
